label: words
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: garden shelter
Length: 30 s: 95-120 words in all, one sentence per beat (11 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 108 words in all, about 10 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 120 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- A 90 mile per hour wind pushes about 20 pounds on every square foot.
- Footings usually go below the frost line, so frost cannot heave them up.
- Paving slabs are laid on a compacted sub-base so they stay flat and drain

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: four posts and a roof appear on the lawn. actions: shelter show (on "posts")
   idea: four posts and a roof on the lawn keep the rain off
   cue words: "posts"
2. problem
   on screen: wind arrows hit it and the shelter tips up on one side. actions: light storm (on "But"); wind show (on "wind"); shelter tip (on "wind")
   idea: the first gust of wind catches the roof and tips the whole thing
   cue words: "But", "wind"
3. fix1
   on screen: the shelter settles back, a trench is dug and concrete footings grow under the front posts. actions: wind hide (on "So"); shelter tipBack (on "So"); dig dig (on "dig"); footings grow (on "concrete"); footings grow (on "concrete"); backfill grow (on "posts")
   idea: dig down and pour concrete footings that hold the posts
   cue words: "So", "dig", "concrete", "posts"
   its fact: Footings usually go below the frost line, so frost cannot heave them up.
4. problem2
   on screen: rain falls and puddles spread under the roof. actions: rain start (on "But"); puddles rise (on "mud")
   idea: under the roof, the grass is walked to mud and puddles
   cue words: "But", "mud"
5. fix2
   on screen: a floor of paving slabs wipes in under the roof. actions: puddles dry (on "So"); slabs grow (on "slabs")
   idea: lay paving slabs for a dry, flat floor
   cue words: "So", "slabs"
   its fact: Paving slabs are laid on a compacted sub-base so they stay flat and drain
6. problem3
   on screen: wind arrows and rain spray blow in sideways across the floor. actions: wind show (on "wind"); spray start (on "sideways")
   idea: the wind blows rain in sideways across the slabs
   cue words: "wind", "sideways"
7. fix3
   on screen: a back wall and a side wall appear and the spray stops. actions: shelter walls (on "wall"); spray stop (on "wall")
   idea: a back wall and a side wall block the wind
   cue words: "wall"
8. name
   on screen: an outline traces the shelter. actions: wind hide; shelter outline show (on "garden")
   idea: this is a garden shelter
   cue words: "garden"
9. fact
   on screen: wind arrows push on the roof and a counter beside it ticks up to 20. actions: shelter outline hide (on "gust"); wind show (on "gust"); stand show (on "gust"); pressure show (on "gust"); pressure count (on "20")
   idea: a strong gust pushes about 20 pounds on every square foot of roof
   cue words: "gust", "20"
   its fact: A 90 mile per hour wind pushes about 20 pounds on every square foot.
10. finish
   on screen: stepping stones and bushes appear, the rain stops. actions: pressure hide (on "Add"); wind hide (on "Add"); rain stop (on "Add"); light clear (on "Add"); stones show (on "stones"); bushes show (on "bushes")
   idea: stepping stones to its door and bushes around it
   cue words: "Add", "stones", "bushes"
11. congrats
   on screen: the finished shelter stands calm in the sun
   idea: you have built a garden shelter
   cue words: (none)
